notes.title: Status update.
notes.notes:
Hello pinball friends!

 

It's time for a new status update.

Not that you think I'm taking a whole month's vacation. 😉

 

No, I'm working hard on the new pinball machine and am currently working on many things at once. That's why it's not so easy to show anything new. Although, the backglass is completely finished and the name of the pinball machine is on it.

Here it is:

 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925975/bfe2197be6c5f88ea031636c5df10cccc01f98b1.png"]

I'm right in the middle of everything else, and it's gradually coming together.

However, I haven't even started on the animations for the DMD yet. I'm curious to see how long it will take me. 😉

I'm saving time on the music because this time it won't be mine. I want orchestral pirate music, which I'm not very good at. That's why I'm buying the pieces from a nice person I know from Twitter (X). I've already picked out a few pieces and can say that it's going to be really good.

So, I'm on the right track and it will take some time.

But that's okay, because it's still summer.

notes.title: Version 0.2.0.5
notes.notes:
Minor adjustments to Monster Pub.
The debug overlay is now disabled at startup.
However, it can still be turned on and off using the F9 key.

notes.title: Version 0.2.0.4 - Updates and bug fixes
notes.notes:
Fight Back 

- New animation file for the DMD added. 
It is now in VP8 container and should work with Linux.

Monster Pub

- Some textures improved.
- Rewrote some parts of the code to prevent an error during “Serve it” where the dish cannot be served. 
Since I was never able to reproduce the error myself, it is possible that the error will continue to occur. 
However, you can now use the F9 key to show and hide a small debug area that displays the status of some important variables. 

If the error occurs, please press F9 and also take a screenshot before the ball goes out. This information could help me with troubleshooting.
Thanks!

notes.title: New version 0.2.0.3
notes.notes:
Starting with this version, the active camera is now displayed.
This always happens after the table has loaded and when a different camera is selected.

In Djinn Pinball, the shield post (the puck between the flipper fingers) has been moved slightly toward the drain. It's now easier to hit the WISH targets while the post is up.

Have Fun!

notes.title: Bugfixes and more
notes.notes:
Monster Pub Pinball:
Fixed a problem with TAA antialiasing that caused the score board to flicker.
Fixed an issue where the ball could get stuck at the exit of the shooter lane.
Slightly reduced the reflection of the glass pane.

All pinbal games in the Time Attack game mode:
The reached score is now transferred to the leaderboard on Steam after each loss of the ball and not only when the 30 minutes are over. This also applies to checking the achievement.

notes.title: Engine update, achievement description, leaderboards.
notes.notes:
Hello pinball friends!

I hope you all had a good start into the new year and are in the mood for an update. ːsteamhappyː

In short: The game engine has been brought up to date. 
The descriptions of the achievements are now displayed.
The leaderboards for each table and game mode are in the game!


Game Engine:

At the start of the new year, I finally carried out a game engine update.
Surprisingly, it worked “almost” without any problems. I only had to rework a few things. 
In the tests I carried out, “I” couldn't notice any negative differences in performance. However, if you notice anything while playing that was better before, please let me know.

Leaderboards:

The leaderboards are finally visible in the menu!
After much deliberation on how best to insert them, I have decided to add an additional window after the game mode selection.
So you select the table, then the game mode and then a new window appears showing the leaderboard for this mode (just one more click to get into the game).
There you can choose between 3 display types.
A Top10 display, where if you are not in the Top10, you will be shown in the 11 line with placement.
A placement display in which you and your competitors are displayed in the area surrounding your position.
And a friends display, where only the best-placed friends and you are shown. 

Achievements:

The descriptions of the Achievements can now be seen in the table selection. So you no longer have to look in Steam to find out when you get an Achievement.

All of these things can of course be accessed using the game pad, keyboard or mouse.  

Have fun!

notes.title: Bugfix on Djinn and some adjustments
notes.notes:
Hello pinball friends!
We have some news.

First a few notes on the update.

Djinn Pinball Table: 
I fixed a bug where a certain multiball would start without activating the jackpots. Also made some minor adjustments that should improve the flow of the game.

Gameplay in general: 
If the ball is on launch, then a shake does not lead to a tilt.
(For people who have placed launch and nudge together on one stick) 

The menus have been made a little more user-friendly. (Roll up/down and left/right) 
Spelling mistakes have been fixed.

And while I'm on the subject of the new table:

Unfortunately, the table is taking longer than I thought. This is mainly because I couldn't use the code from the old pinball machine after all. Because of the multiplayer mode and the caching of all the player data, I had to set up a completely different structure. And the little that I could have used didn't matter.
I may have overdone it a bit with the data.
I really save every state of the player. Missions, targets, lights and even progress within the missions. If, for example, some drop targets were retrieved when the ball went out, they are set up again in exactly the same way when it's the player's turn again.
I didn't have to do that. But that's how it is now! 

I'm doing everything I can to finish the table this year (preferably before Christmas).
The mechanics are in place and working well.
The program is 99.5% complete. (there are still a few minor bugs)
The display does what it should. 
Almost all sounds are in.
Now only the graphics and some effects are missing.
So I'm on the home straight!

Have fun!

notes.title: Bugfixes and new button for gamepads
notes.notes:
Bugfixes for Djinn:

- I fixed a bug where completing the Whish mission during a multiball would cause the 3 ball multiball to not trigger.

- It is possible to shoot 2 balls in quick succession into the ramp to the palace lock. If the first ball rolls slowly and is caught up by the second, both balls are in the lock. The second ball was not registered and so the game hung.
I have fixed this so that both balls are now recognized and are simply released again in such a case.

New input for the gamepad:

The gamepad has now been assigned a button that is responsible for the launch. The gamepad now has an analog launch and a digital one. This is important for the new table which has no plunger.
It is also good for gamepads that only have one analog stick. Putting the preset analog launch on a button means that the plunger is always pulled completely and does not slowly go to its maximum value, as it would with the keyboard.

Attention!!! This button is Button B or Button East. So, if you are already using this button, please rebind the controller so that it works for you.

notes.title: Second update to Only pinball
notes.notes:
Hello pinball friends. 
There's news! 

The most important thing: 

I will start early access in September. ːsteamhappyː

The second pinball table "Djinn" is finished and works very well. So now 2 tables are finished, and they will provide many hours of fun across all game modes!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925975/89e237a37162931ef802727e4fed1877e5d161cc.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925975/79fc33ca1d45fb151d6c5eb33d40b2231b63ecc7.png

I'm currently taking a short summer break. But I still test the pinball machines every day. 
I've also changed a few things here and there to make the gameplay a bit fairer. I'm also trying to get all the achievements, which isn't easy. But that's how it should be.
After the summer break, I will start with the third pinball machine, then using a DMD (dot matrix display) as display. I will create this from scratch because the technology of the DMDs from the old collection is too complicated. Moreover, the new DMDs will be multi-colored.
To save some resources (my labor), I'll be using a pinball machine from the old collection and expanding it. 
I chose "Time To Fight Back" because it's the pinball machine where most players have reached the maximum number of points. For me, that's a sign of how popular the pinball machine is. It's also a wide-body pinball machine, so I can directly integrate a housing of that kind. And I'm really looking forward to redesigning the artwork and lighting, because the original was a bit plain. The rules will largely remain the same, but I'll arrange a few things differently. I've already come up with something nice. I'm going to reduce the number of points you can get in the game by a factor of 10. I'm curious to see whether the maximum number of points can still be reached afterwards.

I already have 3 other themes in mind for future pinball machines: 

Monster Shop - Various monsters want to buy specific things. 

Beat Master - A pinball machine with rhythm and music. 

Soccer Mania - A pinball machine where you can score goals. 

If you have any ideas for new themes or new mechanics that you would like to play, let me know. 
As long as it will be feasible and exciting and not violate copyrights, I could try implementing it for you.

So, now you know what is most important for the moment. Many other things will be added to the collection on the way. But I will announce those separately. 

Keep the silver ball rolling

notes.title: A first update on Only Pinball.
notes.notes:
Hello pinball friends!
It's time for a first update.

I've been busy and programmed almost everything that is needed to run this collection.
Each table will have 3 game modes.
You can choose whether you want to play with 5 balls or 3 balls.
Each table can be played with up to 4 players and you don't have to select this in the menu. Simply press another button when you start the game and the next player is there.
There is a training mode that is played for 30 minutes with unlimited balls and a lamp killer mode where the ball has to roll over the lights. These lights give points and extra time. (you know something similar from Zaccaria)

I'm currently working on the second table.
The pinball machine is called "Djinn" and is based a little on the stories from 1001 Nights.
This table is also a solid state from the late 1980s, so it has a segment display and clear rules.
All objects are built and the lights are set. I've created the table rules and apart from a small bug, everything works.
Sound and music are 98% finished and the textures are 75% finished. So this table won't take much longer.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925975/bdae032d3d1d154901fd7a21db1fc5cc7202523f.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925975/5393646440d09c04278f291fe93095e782fbce94.png
It's cool, isn't it?

What's still missing for both pinball machines are the Steam adjustments and the achievement icons.
When that's all done, I'll start the third table, which will be inspired by the 90s and will have a DMD display.

So things are moving forward!

Unfortunately, it's taking a little longer than Malzbie's Pinball Collection, because the tables are much more realistic and therefore require more work. And as you know, I'm doing it all by myself.

There have been a lot of questions about Only Pinball, so here's a little FAQ.

Are there achievements?

Yes, each table will have 12 achievements. 10 for the normal game, and one each for the training mode and the lamp killer mode.

Are there leaderboards again?

Sure! I'll create a leaderboard for each mode.
One for the 3 ball mode, one for the 5 ball mode, one for the time trial and one for the lamp killer mode.

When will Only Pinball be released?

I can't say exactly yet, but it will be this year.
As soon as all Steam adjustments have been made and the third table is in the works, the shop will be switched to Early Access.
It's important to note that this time there will be no free table and the tables cannot be purchased individually.
No, this time the tables will be added gradually at no additional cost.

Why Early Access and not like the old collection with a free pinball table and DLC?

There are several reasons for this.
- I've noticed that almost all players who bought one pinball table buy all the pinball tables in the collection anyway. There's only a 1% difference in sales figures.
- There are a lot of people who get every free game on Steam, regardless of whether they like it or not. Some of them then give a bad review because they don't even know what a pinball game is. I don't want to see those reviews anymore.
- It's easier for me to develop tables without DLC.

I know that Early Access is only good for those who trust me, want to support me or just want to play right away. Unfortunately, everyone else has to wait until it's finished at some point or they think that the price is worth the content.

Can I at least try out the tables?

Sure! There will be a demo where some tables can be tested. Not all of them, because that would make the demo too big. But it will be a good selection that will allow you to see whether it is fun and, above all, whether it will run on your computer.

How many tables will be included in the collection?

That is still open. This collection actually has no upper limit.
There will be "at least" 10 completely new tables. And I will also include some old tables from Malzbie's Pinball Collection. These tables will be improved and expanded. Maybe there will simply be a successor to a table with new rules. But I don't know that for sure yet.

Tables from the 80s, 90s and modern times, what does that mean?

This means that the tables are set in a certain era and are intended to be a simulation of possible tables. No visual frills like tracers or dispalys of points above the ball.

The tables from the 80s have segment displays and can only display a little information. The rules are kept quite simple and are usually easy to recognize. They are still fun!

The tables from the 90s have a dot matrix display and can display more complex animations and information. The rules are more complex and the layout is more elaborate.

The tables from the modern times are intended to have a monitor as a display medium. But I'm not quite sure whether it will be powerful enough. In any case, the rules and layout will be complex.

Can I request a theme for a table?

Of course! And you should. I want to work with the community and create pinball tables that people want to play. But I won't create a direct copy of a real pinball machine.

How much will it cost?

I don't know that yet either. The price will be somewhere between 10 and 20 (US $/€). You'll see that once Early Access starts. 

So, now you know what to expect. And it's going to be great!
